### How to contribute {.unnumbered}

Instructions for contributors can be found in the OMA
[README](https://github.com/microbiome/OMA/blob/devel/README.md#development-and-contributions).

### Background of the book {.unnumbered}

The framework for microbiome data science presented in this book is based
on specialized data containers for hierarchical and multi-omic data sets.
The `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("TreeSummarizedExperiment")` data container for
single-omic data was created by @R_TreeSummarizedExperiment, and the
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("MultiAssayExperiment")` container for multi-omic
data by @Ramos2017.

The idea of using these containers as a basis for microbiome data science
was initiated by Domenick Braccia, Héctor Corrada Bravo, Felix Ernst, and
others, and brought together with other microbiome data science developers
[@Shetty2019; @Ernst2020]. Setting up the base ecosystem of packages and
tutorials was subsequently led by Tuomas Borman, Felix Ernst, and
[Leo Lahti](http://www.iki.fi/Leo.Lahti). Lahti had earlier developed the
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("phyloseq")`-based
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("microbiome")` R package before switching to the
(Tree)SE/MAE-based framework and the `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")` family of
Bioconductor packages introduced in this book. The
[tidyomics](https://github.com/tidyomics) project [@Hutchison2024] has
since made it easier to build omic data analysis workflows.

Ample data resources have been bridged to the framework through the
[curatedMetagenomicData](https://waldronlab.io/curatedMetagenomicData/)
project by Edoardo Pasolli, Lucas Schiffer, Levi Waldron, and others
[@Pasolli2017], and through the `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("HoloFoodR")` and
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("MGnifyR")` packages.

Many other contributors have since advanced the ecosystem further. Their
work is acknowledged in the individual packages,
[pull requests](https://github.com/microbiome/OMA/graphs/contributors),
[issues](https://github.com/microbiome/OMA/issues), and elsewhere. We thank
everyone who has contributed to this data science ecosystem
(see [@sec-ecosystem]).

For the online book, Christian L. Müller and Stefanie Peschel contributed
chapters on network analysis; Himel Mallick and Nalin Arora on multi-omic
and mediation analyses; and Thomaz F. S. Bastiaanssen and Benjamin
Valderrama to various parts of the book. Jacques Serizay converted the
*OMA* book to the `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("BiocBook")` format, which allows
it to be built and distributed by Bioconductor.

The work drew initial inspiration from many sources, most notably from the
work on `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("phyloseq")` by Paul McMurdie and Susan Holmes
[@McMurdie2013], who pioneered rigorous and reproducible microbiome data
science ecosystems in R/Bioconductor. The `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("phyloseq")`
framework continues to provide a vast array of complementary packages and
methods for microbiome studies. The *Orchestrating Single-Cell Analysis with
Bioconductor* ([*OSCA*](https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA/)) book
by Robert Amezquita, Aaron Lun, Stephanie Hicks, and Raphael Gottardo
[@Amezquita2020natmeth] presents related work on the
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("SummarizedExperiment")` data container and its
derivatives in single-cell sequencing studies, which inspired this work.

The open-source books *Modern Statistics for Modern Biology* by Susan Holmes
and Wolfgang Huber [@Holmes2019], *R for Data Science* by Garrett Grolemund
and Hadley Wickham [@Grolemund2017], and *Statistical Rethinking* by Richard
McElreath, with the associated online resources by Solomon Kurz
[@McElreath2020], are key references that have advanced reproducible data
science training and dissemination.

### Key developers {.unnumbered}

The book and its associated package ecosystem are a highly collaborative
effort involving dozens of developers and contributors.

Contributions to this book are coordinated by **Leo Lahti** and **Tuomas
Borman** at the
[Department of Computing, University of Turku, Finland](https://datascience.utu.fi/).
Both have served on the
[Bioconductor Community Advisory Board](https://bioconductor.org/about/community-advisory-board/)
and run regular international training workshops in microbiome data
science.

Other key developers include Giulio Benedetti, Muluh Geraldson, Himel
Mallick, and Thomaz F. S. Bastiaanssen. The full list of contributors is
available on
[GitHub](https://github.com/microbiome/OMA/graphs/contributors).
